notify_automation_event Postgres RPC (automation event bus)
Destructive test-data wipe of all transactional and master tables
Hardcoded confirmation token is the only guard on the destructive wipe
Delete order hand-written to respect foreign keys: dependents, then transactional, then master data
Sequence resets deliberately skipped: raw SQL execution avoided from the edge function for security
Per-table failures are logged and skipped, so a partial wipe is a normal outcome rather than an error
Wipe is not tenant-scoped: the neq('id', zero-uuid) filter matches every tenant's rows
The cleanup itself is recorded in audit_logs, best-effort so audit failure never fails the wipe
CheckMyDriver (Modives) driver-licence verification provisioning
Three-call Modives handshake: verification -> verification-detail -> consumer-magic-link
Magic-link fan-out across email / SMS / WhatsApp channels, best-effort and non-fatal
Modives compliance: never persist carrier or policy data, only IDs, status enum and the link
The Drive247 Modives account is configured not to auto-email consumers, so link delivery is entirely ours
applicantVerificationReqGuidId lives in result.applicants[0]; a top-level UUID fallback would grab the dealerGuid
Env-var and dealer_guid preflight returns an actionable 503 instead of a generic fetch 500
Magic link and a 7-day expiry are persisted specifically so the link can be re-sent later
CMD results proxy trimmed to licence-only fields for the portal CMD tab
Caller MUST NOT persist this response; insurance/carrier data is dropped before returning
Results and licence document fetched with Promise.allSettled so one failing endpoint still returns the other
CMD verification-status proxy used by the portal during link-sent to verifying polling
The webhook is the source of truth; polling only smooths webhook delivery latency
Cron reconciler that mirrors the CMD webhook's DB updates when no webhook is wired up
Idempotent by design: only provider='cmd' rows still Pending; unschedule the cron and it becomes a no-op
Modives returns mixed casing per endpoint; normalise to the Pascal-case values the webhook stores
Polled updates are logged as 'polled-sync' into the webhook's own audit table for troubleshooting
Modives answers isSuccess:false while the customer is still mid magic-link flow; skip silently
Re-send the stored CMD magic link without creating a new verification
An expired magic link returns 410 and forces a fresh verification run
Channels actually delivered are merged into the stored cmd_delivery_channels set
Modives CheckMyDriver webhook ingestion (verify_jwt = false)
HMAC signature verified against the raw body before any JSON parsing
Licence status drives the verification state machine: Valid -> approved/GREEN, Invalid|Expired -> declined/RED
Insurance (object_type=Verification) events are stored but never surfaced, per the licence-only product scope
Return 200 even on an unmatched uuid or a failed update so Modives does not retry-storm
Every payload is audited (signature pass or fail) for debugging and resync
Accepts both Payload/Header/Body and lower-case payload/header/body envelopes
Modives' body.uuid equals cmd_applicant_verification_id — the join key back to the row create-verification wrote
Deterministic heuristic lead scoring (V1) from booking application data
Score bands hot/warm/cold/risk, with a violations penalty forcing 'risk' below 50
The heuristic is explicitly a V1 placeholder; Phase 3 will plug in ML
Gig/rideshare purpose list (uber, lyft, doordash, instacart, delivery) drives its own signals and penalties
Stateless scorer: no DB, no tenant lookup, no persistence — the caller stores the score
Lead -> customer -> rental conversion pipeline with the conversation preserved
rentals CHECK constraints are casing-sensitive; the old 'Confirmed'/'Paid'/'weekly' values failed the insert silently after the customer was created
Idempotent only when customer_id AND converted_to_rental_id are both set; a vanished rental is healed by recreating it
Reuse an existing customer by lead.customer_id or tenant-scoped email so repeat applicants do not duplicate
auth.users must be reached via the admin API; the PostgREST builder is a thenable with no .catch, which crashed the old attempt
Never roll back by deleting the customer — they may hold prior rentals (the GHULMA half-conversion)
Conversion stops running/waiting lead automations so the converted lead is not still being nurtured
The conversation keeps its lead_id and gains customer_id, so chat history survives conversion
rental.created emitted explicitly via RPC because DB triggers watch leads, not rentals
customers.is_gig_driver derived from the application's purpose against the same gig-platform list used by lead scoring
Bulk creation of a rental's additional drivers
service_role bypasses RLS, so tenant ownership is re-enforced in-function against app_users.tenant_id
Veriff session + invite email are delegated to send-additional-driver-invite so the rental form can fire-and-forget
Pre-write validation mirroring DB constraints: name required, email-or-phone, unique emails, never the primary customer's email
Single batch insert so partial creation cannot happen; unique-violation 23505 mapped to a friendly 409
AI identity-verification QR session provisioning (3-hour expiry, mobile /verify/{token} page)
Rate limit of 10 verification sessions per customer per hour, deliberately fail-open on error
Booking-flow sessions carry no customer_id and are auto-linked later by lowercased customer_email
Two entry shapes in one function: portal (existing customerId) and booking (customerDetails, pre-customer)
Portal flow stamps customers.identity_verification_status = pending as the UI's live signal
Rental agreement generation and BoldSign e-signature dispatch
Agreement template variable substitution engine with {{#if}} conditional pre-pass
Local mileage logic once printed 'Unlimited' whenever an allowance was unset, contractually granting unlimited mileage
PAYG period-rate divisor table duplicated from the portal and must stay in lockstep with payg-rate.ts
Only is_gig_driver and is_payg conditionals are supported, and must match the portal's replaceVariables
apps/portal/src/lib/template-variables.ts — the editor-preview mirror of this substitution engine
Bonzah insurer-mandated addendum gated on tenants.integration_bonzah, resolving to empty for other tenants
Installment payment schedule rendered into the agreement from the rental's plan and scheduled rows
Additional drivers become secondary BoldSign signers and are stamped signing_status='sent'
BoldSign SignerIndex is 1-based in TextTagDefinitions but 0-based in the Signers[] array
Dedup guard skips creation when the rental already carries a non-terminal agreement, saving sandbox quota
The BoldSign document id is stored in the legacy rentals.docusign_envelope_id column
Blocking credit deduction before send, refund on BoldSign failure, non-blocking auto-refill after
DisableEmails=true: the platform sends its own signing email and WhatsApp instead of BoldSign's
DOB, licence number and expiry fall back to the newest identity_verifications row when the customer record is blank
The tenant's own published terms are fetched and spliced in as {{terms_and_conditions}}
Per-tenant BoldSign test/live mode and brand id resolved per request, mirroring the Stripe dual-mode pattern
General rental payment Stripe Checkout session creation (booking and portal)
Zero or non-finite totals rejected: Stripe accepts a 0-amount line item and its completion still fires the webhook
Tenant resolved by slug, then body id, then via the rental — three fallbacks for three caller shapes
Any non-null rentals.deposit_amount_override wins, including an explicit 0 meaning the operator opted out
Auto-extend or already-extended rentals carry no deposit at all, overriding every other source
Deposit-hold disclosure surfaced as Stripe Checkout custom_text next to the Pay button
Stored Stripe customer ids are account+mode scoped and must be validated before reuse or sessions.create 'No such customer's
Category-targeted and extension flows must INSERT a dedicated payment row, never reuse a generic Pending one
Account-level collect-then-decide: money lands as unallocated customer credit instead of FIFO onto charges
place_deposit_hold metadata tells the Stripe webhook to authorise the deposit off-session on the saved card
Charge platform chosen from the tenant's payment model: managed tenants on the legacy UK account, own tenants on UAE
Stripe Connect Express account creation and onboarding-link generation
Connect onboarding always uses the live secret key regardless of the tenant's Stripe mode, and 503s if it is missing
stripe_account_id, stripe_account_status='pending' and stripe_onboarding_complete=false stamped on the tenant
Platform credit-wallet top-up checkout
One shared Supabase auth project means a valid JWT proves nothing about tenant membership — every rental customer holds one
Credits always bill on the UAE Stripe account for every tenant, because they are one-time with no saved-card dependency
uae_customer_id versus stripe_subscription_customer_id: never clobber the column the subscription webhook resolves invoices with
Selecting a non-existent tenants column silently nulled the row and minted a fresh Stripe customer on every purchase
Write-once platform-ToS acceptance stamped on the tenant, enforced by the .is(null) filter rather than a pre-read
ToS acceptance mirrored into Stripe session metadata so a failed DB write leaves a recoverable trace
Minimum credit purchase exists because the AED-settling account rejects sessions under ~200 fils
Without .select() PostgREST answers 204 with no body, making a 'recorded' audit log line unfalsifiable
Tenant-scoped customer registration invite token with 7-day expiry
Caller must be an app_user of the target tenant (or super admin) before an invite can be minted
Invite URL convention: https://{tenantSlug}.drive-247.com/register/{token} on the booking app
Idempotent demo admin bootstrap (create-or-locate, then force password and confirmation)
Demo user is deliberately created with tenant_id NULL — a global admin identity for testing
Hardcoded admin@demo.com / demo123 credentials returned in the response body
Existing user located by paging admin.listUsers with a case-insensitive email compare
Server-authoritative rental-extension checkout reading amounts from the rental_extensions row
Deprecated legacy path synthesises a rental_extensions row and parks the lump sum entirely in rental_amount
A paid extension 409s and a zero-total extension 400s before any Stripe call
extension_id and the four Extension target_categories stamped on the payment so apply-payment routes deterministically
Legacy rentals.extension_checkout_url / extension_amount kept in sync until the UI migrates off them
bonzah_policy_id stamped on the extension so the insurance quote is confirmed after Stripe succeeds, not before
Manual security-deposit hold checkout (authorise only, capture_method='manual')
Endpoint was reachable with the public anon key shipped in the booking bundle, so any session could mint sessions on any tenant's Stripe account
deposit_hold_status is never revisited, so an expired authorisation left operators permanently unable to place a new hold
Any doubt about hold liveness resolves to 'alive' so a customer's card is never double-authorised
Stale-status heal is anchored to the exact status and PaymentIntent probed, because the refresh cron replaces PIs underneath
Graduated card-feature fallback: extended_authorization + multicapture, then extended only, then neither
Manual hold once ignored deposit_mode and under-held every per-vehicle-priced rental; now uses the shared resolver
Dead-PaymentIntent status map duplicated in place-deposit-hold on purpose, to avoid touching the shared Stripe client
Auto-extend rentals never carry a deposit; manually extended ones are still allowed because this is a deliberate staff action
The existing hold is probed on the platform account it was CREATED on, which may differ from where a new hold would go
Installment plan creation plus a fees-and-first-installment Stripe Checkout session
Splittable = base + tax + service fee; insurance and booking/delivery fees are always upfront; the deposit is out of band
interval_days = (week 7 | month 30) / paymentsPerUnit, with a human frequency label stored in plan config
Rounding remainder is soaked up by the final installment so the schedule always sums to the installable amount
Back-compat shim translating legacy planType/baseUpfrontAmount into unit + paymentsPerUnit + upfrontFixedAmount
Checkout metadata carries plan and installment ids so the Stripe webhook can settle installment #1 via installment_settle_invoice
Only one active or pending installment plan per rental is permitted
The rental is tagged has_installment_plan + installment_plan_id so downstream readers find the plan
